assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The period analysed is 17 September 2026, compared with the preceding period of equal length; the evidence compares 17-18 September against the baseline week of 10-16 September.
caveats: The comparison window covers 17-18 September, and the outage ran past the end of 17 September, so some of the impact falls on 18 September rather than 17 September alone.
Hourly rates for Kestrel Bank cards rest on small hourly volumes (often tens of attempts), so individual hours are noisy.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 3.10pp, from 90.07% (83,268 attempts, 10-16 Sep) to 86.98% (22,790 attempts, 17-18 Sep). The change is statistically and practically significant.
The daily series flags a drop window of 17-18 September. The lowest day was 18 September at 86.66%, against a median daily rate of 89.72%.
Kestrel Bank is the segment that concentrates the drop most strongly (strongest segment signal among all dimensions scanned).

Within Kestrel Bank, debit cards fell 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit cards fell 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.80%). UPI, wallet and netbanking at Kestrel Bank showed no significant change.
For Kestrel Bank card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
Across all traffic, ACQ_TIMEOUT rose from 0.08 to 3.58 per 100 attempts (815 failures in the current window), the largest shift of any failure code.

The Kestrel Bank card timeline shows an outage window from 2026-09-17 10:00 to 2026-09-18 22:00 (36 hours). The worst hour was 2026-09-18 02:00 at a 36.36% success rate, against a reference rate of 86.87%. The window accounts for 716 excess failed attempts out of 2,229 affected attempts.
At the overall level, card methods fell about 9 to 10pp (card EMI -9.52pp, debit card -9.28pp, credit card -9.18pp). UPI was essentially unchanged (-0.14pp, not significant).
The data-quality scan found no issues (0 findings).

response.headline: Success rate fell about 3.1pp, from 90.07% to 86.98%, across 17-18 September versus the prior week. It was an acquirer problem, not a mix shift: card payments routed through Kestrel Bank started failing on timeouts from 10:00 on 17 September.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check Kestrel Bank's incident or status reports and gateway logs for card-route latency around 17 Sep 10:00 to 18 Sep 22:00, and confirm with the acquirer relationship contact.
hypotheses.rationale: The drop is concentrated in one acquirer and in card methods only. The only failure code that moved materially is ACQ_TIMEOUT, and the timeline shows a sharp start at 10:00 on 17 September. Non-card methods at the same acquirer were unaffected.
hypotheses.text: An outage or degradation on Kestrel Bank's card processing path (acquirer-side timeouts) caused the drop.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: An outage or degradation on Kestrel Bank's card processing path (acquirer-side timeouts) caused the drop.
recommendations.rationale: ACQ_TIMEOUT on Kestrel Bank cards accounts for most of the shortfall, and the excess failures (716) are material.
recommendations.text: Raise an incident with Kestrel Bank and request a root-cause analysis for the card timeouts between 17 Sep 10:00 and 18 Sep 22:00.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Within Kestrel Bank, debit cards fell 30.11pp (86.42% to 56.31%), credit cards fell 28.71pp (88.64% to 59.94%) and card EMI fell 23.87pp (80.67% to 56.80%). UPI, wallet and netbanking at Kestrel Bank showed no significant change.
recommendations.rationale: The timeout pattern was sustained for 36 hours, so automated failover would have limited the impact.
recommendations.text: Review failover or smart-routing rules so card traffic can shift to an alternate acquirer automatically when ACQ_TIMEOUT spikes.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: For Kestrel Bank card payments, ACQ_TIMEOUT failures rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts (803 failures in the current window). Other failure codes were flat or lower.
recommendations.rationale: The rate rose from 0.26 to 32.27 per 100 attempts at Kestrel Bank cards, a signal that would have been detectable within hours.
recommendations.text: Add an alert on ACQ_TIMEOUT per 100 attempts by acquirer and payment method.
